newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end down sharply, surpassing U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end down sharply, surpassing U.S..

text.p: Canadian bonds fell further than U.S. bonds in quiet trading ahead of the New Year's Day holiday on Wednesday, bond analysts said.
They said U.S. treasuries fell on stronger than expected new home sales and rise in consumer confidence.
"There were a few bearish arguments and that allowed for some bettter selling," said Geoff Hall, fixed income analyst at Technical Data in Boston.
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$1.40 to C$111.35 to yield 7.046 percent, compared to a yield of 6.64 percent for the U.S. 30-year which dropped 1-11/32 to 98.04/32.
New home sales in the U.S. in November rose to an annual rate of 772,000 units from a revised 676,000 in October.
In economic news this morning the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index of New York area business conditions rose to 72.9 in December from 64.9 in November.
Traders said they awaited Chicago purchasing numbers at 1000 EST/1500 GMT before a reaction if any, was likely.
Canada's 10-year bond fell C$0.10 to C$105.15 to yield 6.292 percent, while the nation's two-year benchmark dropped C$0.18 to C$103.53 to yield 4.074 percent.
